page: Amazon Web Services i3.large is an entry-tier storage-optimized virtual machine operating on the Xen hypervisor. It is driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with x86_64 architecture running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via two threads per core, 15.0 GB of system RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. A key feature of this profile is the inclusion of 475 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. The server does not include GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the generational constraints of the Broadwell-era processor. Synthetic compute tests rank in the lower performance brackets, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 866.0, a multi-core score of 1005.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 2202.24. Memory throughput aligns with these results, yielding 11.11 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 7.41 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth. Operational workload metrics demonstrate 1.27 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 1.51 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the i3.large is its low computational density juxtaposed against fast local NVMe storage capacity. While not suited for compute-heavy workloads or modern instruction-set acceleration such as AVX-512, its direct NVMe attachment provides high I/O throughput and low-latency disk access. The instance is suited for localized I/O-bound services, such as small relational databases, distributed NoSQL nodes, search indexers, transactional logs, and persistent caching systems.
